[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai1_UseAssistantMessageBuilder]
=== Use `AssistantMessage.Builder` instead of constructor
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai1.UseAssistantMessageBuilder`

Replace `new AssistantMessage(...)` with `AssistantMessage.builder()....build()`.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.AssistantMessage;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

class Demo {
    void test() {
        AssistantMessage message1 = new AssistantMessage("content");
        AssistantMessage message2 = new AssistantMessage("content", Map.of());
        AssistantMessage message3 = new AssistantMessage("content", Map.of(), List.of());
        AssistantMessage message4 = new AssistantMessage("content", Map.of(), List.of(), List.of());
    }
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.AssistantMessage;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

class Demo {
    void test() {
        AssistantMessage message1 = AssistantMessage.builder().content("content").build();
        AssistantMessage message2 = AssistantMessage.builder().content("content").properties(Map.of()).build();
        AssistantMessage message3 = AssistantMessage.builder().content("content").properties(Map.of()).toolCalls(List.of()).build();
        AssistantMessage message4 = AssistantMessage.builder().content("content").properties(Map.of()).toolCalls(List.of()).media(List.of()).build();
    }
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_MigrateSpringAiChatMemoryToSessionMemory]
=== Migrate Spring AI chat memory to session memory
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.MigrateSpringAiChatMemoryToSessionMemory`

Migrate an application that uses the auto-configured JDBC chat memory, deprecated in Spring AI 2.1, to the session memory that replaces it. The recipe swaps the JDBC chat memory starter for the JDBC session starter, renames the JDBC repository properties, replaces `MessageChatMemoryAdvisor` with the session advisors reading the same 20-message window, and moves the `ChatMemory` bean and its `get` and `clear` calls to `SessionService`. It applies to the whole project or not at all, and only when every chat memory usage maps one to one onto session memory, so a project with another chat memory store, a chat memory or repository built in code, or direct appends to the chat memory is left unchanged. Conversations already stored in the chat memory table are not carried over, since session memory uses its own tables. Run it on a project that is already on Spring AI 2.1.

_Tags: spring, ai_

.Recipes applied
[%collapsible]
====
* Change Gradle or Maven dependency (`org.openrewrite.java.dependencies.ChangeDependency`)
* xref:recipe-catalog/rewrite-spring-core.adoc#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot_properties_RenameSpringBootPropertyKey[Rename Spring Boot configuration property key] (`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot.properties.RenameSpringBootPropertyKey` ×3)
* xref:recipe-catalog/rewrite-spring-core.adoc#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot_properties_CommentSpringBootProperty[Add a comment to a Spring Boot configuration property] (`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot.properties.CommentSpringBootProperty`)
* Replace constant with another constant (`org.openrewrite.java.ReplaceConstantWithAnotherConstant`)
* xref:recipe-catalog/rewrite-spring.adoc#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_UseSpringAiSessionAdvisors[Use the Spring AI session advisors instead of `MessageChatMemoryAdvisor`] (`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.UseSpringAiSessionAdvisors`)
* Change method name (`org.openrewrite.java.ChangeMethodName` ×2)
* Change type (`org.openrewrite.java.ChangeType`)
====

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
package com.example;

import java.util.List;

import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.ChatClient;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.MessageChatMemoryAdvisor;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.memory.ChatMemory;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message;

class ChatService {

    private final ChatClient chatClient;

    private final ChatMemory chatMemory;

    ChatService(ChatClient.Builder chatClientBuilder, ChatMemory chatMemory) {
        this.chatClient = chatClientBuilder
                .defaultAdvisors(MessageChatMemoryAdvisor.builder(chatMemory).build())
                .build();
        this.chatMemory = chatMemory;
    }

    String chat(String conversationId, String message) {
        return chatClient.prompt()
                .user(message)
                .advisors(advisors -> advisors.param(ChatMemory.CONVERSATION_ID, conversationId))
                .call()
                .content();
    }

    List<Message> history(String conversationId) {
        return chatMemory.get(conversationId);
    }

    void reset(String conversationId) {
        chatMemory.clear(conversationId);
    }

}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
package com.example;

import java.util.List;

import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.ChatClient;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.api.MemoryAdvisor;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message;
import org.springframework.ai.session.EventFilter;
import org.springframework.ai.session.SessionService;
import org.springframework.ai.session.advisor.SessionAdvisors;

class ChatService {

    private final ChatClient chatClient;

    private final SessionService chatMemory;

    ChatService(ChatClient.Builder chatClientBuilder, SessionService chatMemory) {
        this.chatClient = chatClientBuilder
                .defaultAdvisors(SessionAdvisors.builder(chatMemory).memory(memory -> memory.eventFilter(EventFilter.lastN(20))).build())
                .build();
        this.chatMemory = chatMemory;
    }

    String chat(String conversationId, String message) {
        return chatClient.prompt()
                .user(message)
                .advisors(advisors -> advisors.param(MemoryAdvisor.CONVERSATION_ID, conversationId))
                .call()
                .content();
    }

    List<Message> history(String conversationId) {
        return chatMemory.getActiveMessages(conversationId);
    }

    void reset(String conversationId) {
        chatMemory.delete(conversationId);
    }

}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_MigrateSpringAiMcp_2_1]
=== Migrate the Spring AI MCP module to Spring AI 2.1
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.MigrateSpringAiMcp_2_1`

Update usages of Spring AI MCP APIs that were deprecated for removal in Spring AI 2.1. The `toolCallExceptionClass` parameter of the MCP tool method callbacks is no longer used, since exception dispatch became type-based in Spring AI 2.0.1, so the constructors that accept it give way to the three-argument ones.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import java.lang.reflect.Method;

import org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.method.tool.AsyncMcpToolMethodCallback;
import org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.method.tool.ReturnMode;
import org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.method.tool.SyncMcpToolMethodCallback;

class Demo {
    SyncMcpToolMethodCallback sync(Method method, Object provider) {
        return new SyncMcpToolMethodCallback(ReturnMode.TEXT, method, provider, Exception.class);
    }

    AsyncMcpToolMethodCallback async(Method method, Object provider) {
        return new AsyncMcpToolMethodCallback(ReturnMode.TEXT, method, provider, RuntimeException.class);
    }
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import java.lang.reflect.Method;

import org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.method.tool.AsyncMcpToolMethodCallback;
import org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.method.tool.ReturnMode;
import org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.method.tool.SyncMcpToolMethodCallback;

class Demo {
    SyncMcpToolMethodCallback sync(Method method, Object provider) {
        return new SyncMcpToolMethodCallback(ReturnMode.TEXT, method, provider);
    }

    AsyncMcpToolMethodCallback async(Method method, Object provider) {
        return new AsyncMcpToolMethodCallback(ReturnMode.TEXT, method, provider);
    }
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_FindMigratableSpringAiChatMemory]
=== Find projects whose Spring AI chat memory can be migrated to session memory
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.FindMigratableSpringAiChatMemory`

Find the source files of a project that uses the auto-configured JDBC chat memory only in ways that map one to one onto Spring AI session memory. A project that uses another chat memory store, builds or implements a chat memory or repository in code, appends messages to the chat memory directly, or holds a `MessageChatMemoryAdvisor` outside a `ChatClient` advisors call does not qualify.

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_UseChatOptionsBuilder]
=== Pass `ChatOptions.Builder` to `ChatClient` options methods
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.UseChatOptionsBuilder`

Remove `.build()` from `ChatOptions` builder chains passed to `ChatClient.options()` and `ChatClient.Builder.defaultOptions()`, as these methods now accept `ChatOptions.Builder` directly in Spring AI 2.0.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.ChatClient;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.prompt.ChatOptions;

class Demo {
    void test(ChatClient chatClient) {
        chatClient.prompt()
                .options(ChatOptions.builder()
                        .temperature(0.2)
                        .build())
                .call()
                .content();
    }
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.ai.chat.client.ChatClient;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.prompt.ChatOptions;

class Demo {
    void test(ChatClient chatClient) {
        chatClient.prompt()
                .options(ChatOptions.builder()
                        .temperature(0.2))
                .call()
                .content();
    }
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_UseOpenAiResponseFormatBuilder]
=== Use `OpenAiChatModel.ResponseFormat.builder(...)` instead of constructor
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.UseOpenAiResponseFormatBuilder`

Replace `new ResponseFormat(type, jsonSchema)` with `OpenAiChatModel.ResponseFormat.builder().type(type).jsonSchema(jsonSchema).build()`.

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_UseOpenAiEmbeddingEncodingFormatEnum]
=== Use `OpenAiEmbeddingOptions.EncodingFormat` enum constants
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.UseOpenAiEmbeddingEncodingFormatEnum`

Replace `OpenAiEmbeddingOptions.Builder.encodingFormat(String)` literal calls such as `.encodingFormat("float")` with the matching `OpenAiEmbeddingOptions.EncodingFormat` enum constant.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.ai.openai.OpenAiEmbeddingOptions;

class Demo {
    OpenAiEmbeddingOptions test() {
        return OpenAiEmbeddingOptions.builder()
                .encodingFormat("float")
                .build();
    }
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.ai.openai.OpenAiEmbeddingOptions;

class Demo {
    OpenAiEmbeddingOptions test() {
        return OpenAiEmbeddingOptions.builder()
                .encodingFormat(OpenAiEmbeddingOptions.EncodingFormat.FLOAT)
                .build();
    }
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_ai2_UseSpringAiSessionAdvisors]
=== Use the Spring AI session advisors instead of `MessageChatMemoryAdvisor`
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.ai2.UseSpringAiSessionAdvisors`

Replace a `MessageChatMemoryAdvisor` passed to a `ChatClient` advisors method with the advisors built by `SessionAdvisors`, reading the same 20-message window as the auto-configured chat memory and keeping the advisor order. Other advisors passed in the same call stay in place, and the session advisors move to a call of their own.

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot4_MigrateSpringBootRabbitMq_4_2]
=== Migrate the Spring Boot AMQP module to the RabbitMQ module in Spring Boot 4.2
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot4.MigrateSpringBootRabbitMq_4_2`

Keep an application on AMQP 0.9 when upgrading to Spring Boot 4.2 by moving from the AMQP starter and module, which now provide AMQP 1.0 support, to the RabbitMQ starter and module. Adopting AMQP 1.0 instead is a separate, manual migration to the `spring-boot-starter-amqp-rabbitmq` starter.

_Tags: spring, boot_

.Recipes applied
[%collapsible]
====
* Change Gradle or Maven dependency (`org.openrewrite.java.dependencies.ChangeDependency` ×3)
* Rename package name (`org.openrewrite.java.ChangePackage` ×5)
====

*Example*

.Before
[source,groovy]
----
plugins {
    id 'java-library'
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    implementation "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-amqp"
    implementation "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-amqp"
    testImplementation "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-amqp-test"
}
----

.After
[source,groovy]
----
plugins {
    id 'java-library'
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    implementation "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-rabbitmq"
    implementation "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-rabbitmq"
    testImplementation "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-rabbitmq-test"
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot4_MigrateSpringBootHttp_4_2]
=== Migrate the Spring Boot HTTP modules to Spring Boot 4.2
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot4.MigrateSpringBootHttp_4_2`

Update usages of Spring Boot HTTP module APIs that were removed or replaced in Spring Boot 4.2. The `HttpMessageConverters` class removed from the HTTP Converter module is replaced with the Spring Framework interface of the same name. Both are iterable over the configured converters. Code that constructs the removed class needs to be reworked manually around the Spring Framework builders.

_Tags: spring, boot_

.Recipes applied
[%collapsible]
====
* Change type (`org.openrewrite.java.ChangeType`)
====

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.boot.http.converter.autoconfigure.HttpMessageConverters;
import org.springframework.http.converter.HttpMessageConverter;

class Demo {
    void test(HttpMessageConverters converters) {
        for (HttpMessageConverter<?> converter : converters) {
            System.out.println(converter);
        }
    }
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.http.converter.HttpMessageConverter;
import org.springframework.http.converter.HttpMessageConverters;

class Demo {
    void test(HttpMessageConverters converters) {
        for (HttpMessageConverter<?> converter : converters) {
            System.out.println(converter);
        }
    }
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot4_AddAutoConfigureRestTestClientAnnotation]
=== Add missing `@AutoConfigureRestTestClient` annotation
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot4.AddAutoConfigureRestTestClientAnnotation`

Add missing `@AutoConfigureRestTestClient` annotation to classes annotated with `@SpringBootTest` or `@WebMvcTest` that use `RestTestClient`.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.client.RestTestClient;

@SpringBootTest
class MyControllerTest {
  @Autowired
  private RestTestClient restTestClient;
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.resttestclient.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureRestTestClient;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.client.RestTestClient;

@AutoConfigureRestTestClient
@SpringBootTest
class MyControllerTest {
  @Autowired
  private RestTestClient restTestClient;
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot4_AddAutoConfigureTestRestTemplateAnnotation]
=== Add missing `@AutoConfigureTestRestTemplate` annotation
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot4.AddAutoConfigureTestRestTemplateAnnotation`

Add missing `@AutoConfigureTestRestTemplate` annotation to classes annotated with `@SpringBootTest` or `@WebMvcTest` that use `TestRestTemplate`.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.resttestclient.TestRestTemplate;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;

@SpringBootTest
class MyControllerTest {
  @Autowired
  private TestRestTemplate testRestTemplate;
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.resttestclient.TestRestTemplate;
import org.springframework.boot.resttestclient.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureTestRestTemplate;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;

@AutoConfigureTestRestTemplate
@SpringBootTest
class MyControllerTest {
  @Autowired
  private TestRestTemplate testRestTemplate;
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot4_AddAutoConfigureWebTestClientAnnotation]
=== Add missing `@AutoConfigureWebTestClient` annotation
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot4.AddAutoConfigureWebTestClientAnnotation`

Add missing `@AutoConfigureWebTestClient` annotation to classes annotated with `@SpringBootTest` or `@WebMvcTest` that use `WebTestClient`.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.reactive.server.WebTestClient;

@SpringBootTest
class MyControllerTest {
  @Autowired
  private WebTestClient webTestClient;
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.webtestclient.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureWebTestClient;
import org.springframework.test.web.reactive.server.WebTestClient;

@AutoConfigureWebTestClient
@SpringBootTest
class MyControllerTest {
  @Autowired
  private WebTestClient webTestClient;
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_cloud2026_MigrateSpringCloudConfig_5_1]
=== Migrate Spring Cloud Config to 5.1
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.cloud2026.MigrateSpringCloudConfig_5_1`

Migrate Spring Cloud Config usages that changed in the 5.1 release shipped with Spring Cloud 2026.0. Config Client retry moved from Spring Retry to the retry support built into Spring Framework, and it is no longer enabled by having Spring Retry on the classpath. In a module that uses the Config Client and depends on Spring Retry, the recipe sets `spring.cloud.config.retry.enabled=true` in the configuration files that set `spring.cloud.config.fail-fast`, so retry stays enabled, and removes the Spring Retry dependency unless the code uses it.

.Recipes applied
[%collapsible]
====
* xref:recipe-catalog/rewrite-spring-core.adoc#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_boot_properties_AddSpringBootProperty[Add a Spring Boot configuration property] (`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.boot.properties.AddSpringBootProperty`)
* Remove a Gradle or Maven dependency (`org.openrewrite.java.dependencies.RemoveDependency`)
====

*Example*

.Before
[source,properties]
----
spring.config.import=configserver:http://localhost:8888
spring.cloud.config.fail-fast=true
spring.cloud.config.retry.max-attempts=10
----

.After
[source,properties]
----
spring.config.import=configserver:http://localhost:8888
spring.cloud.config.fail-fast=true
spring.cloud.config.retry.enabled=true
spring.cloud.config.retry.max-attempts=10
----

.Before
[source,yaml]
----
spring:
  cloud:
    config:
      fail-fast: true
      retry:
        max-attempts: 10
---
spring:
  config:
    activate:
      on-profile: local
    import: "optional:configserver:"
----

.After
[source,yaml]
----
spring:
  cloud:
    config:
      fail-fast: true
      retry:
        max-attempts: 10
        enabled: true
---
spring:
  config:
    activate:
      on-profile: local
    import: "optional:configserver:"
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_cloud2026_MigrateSpringCloudGateway_5_1]
=== Migrate Spring Cloud Gateway to 5.1
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.cloud2026.MigrateSpringCloudGateway_5_1`

Migrate Spring Cloud Gateway usages that changed in the 5.1 release shipped with Spring Cloud 2026.0. The retry filter moved from Reactor Addons to the retry support built into Reactor, dropping the `basedOnPreviousValue` backoff flag.

.Recipes applied
[%collapsible]
====
* Delete method argument (`org.openrewrite.java.DeleteMethodArgument` ×2)
====

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import java.time.Duration;

import org.springframework.cloud.gateway.filter.factory.RetryGatewayFilterFactory;

class Demo {
    RetryGatewayFilterFactory.RetryConfig config = new RetryGatewayFilterFactory.RetryConfig()
            .setBackoff(Duration.ofMillis(10), Duration.ofMillis(50), 2, false);

    RetryGatewayFilterFactory.BackoffConfig backoff =
            new RetryGatewayFilterFactory.BackoffConfig(Duration.ofMillis(10), Duration.ofMillis(50), 2, true);
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import java.time.Duration;

import org.springframework.cloud.gateway.filter.factory.RetryGatewayFilterFactory;

class Demo {
    RetryGatewayFilterFactory.RetryConfig config = new RetryGatewayFilterFactory.RetryConfig()
            .setBackoff(Duration.ofMillis(10), Duration.ofMillis(50), 2);

    RetryGatewayFilterFactory.BackoffConfig backoff =
            new RetryGatewayFilterFactory.BackoffConfig(Duration.ofMillis(10), Duration.ofMillis(50), 2);
}
----

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.data.annotation.PersistenceConstructor;
import org.springframework.data.mapping.PersistentEntity;
import org.springframework.data.mapping.PersistentProperty;
import org.springframework.data.mapping.PersistentPropertyPath;
import org.springframework.data.mapping.PropertyPath;
import org.springframework.data.util.TypeInformation;

class Person {

    @PersistenceConstructor
    Person(String name) {
    }

    PropertyPath path = PropertyPath.from("name", Person.class);
    TypeInformation<Person> type = null;

    boolean creatorArgument(PersistentEntity<?, ?> entity, PersistentProperty<?> property) {
        return entity.isConstructorArgument(property);
    }

    PersistentProperty<?> leaf(PersistentPropertyPath<PersistentProperty<?>> path) {
        return path.getRequiredLeafProperty();
    }
}

[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.data.annotation.PersistenceCreator;
import org.springframework.data.core.PropertyPath;
import org.springframework.data.core.TypeInformation;
import org.springframework.data.mapping.PersistentEntity;
import org.springframework.data.mapping.PersistentProperty;
import org.springframework.data.mapping.PersistentPropertyPath;

class Person {

    @PersistenceCreator
    Person(String name) {
    }

    PropertyPath path = PropertyPath.from("name", Person.class);
    TypeInformation<Person> type = null;

    boolean creatorArgument(PersistentEntity<?, ?> entity, PersistentProperty<?> property) {
        return entity.isCreatorArgument(property);
    }

    PersistentProperty<?> leaf(PersistentPropertyPath<PersistentProperty<?>> path) {
        return path.getLeafProperty();
    }
}
----

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.web.filter.ForwardedHeaderFilter;
import org.springframework.web.server.adapter.ForwardedHeaderTransformer;

        return new ForwardedHeaderFilter();
    }

}

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.web.filter.ForwardedHeaderFilter;
import org.springframework.web.server.adapter.ForwardedHeaderTransformer;

class Demo {
    ForwardedHeaderFilter filter() {
        return new ForwardedHeaderFilter(false);
    }

    ForwardedHeaderTransformer transformer() {
        return new ForwardedHeaderTransformer(false);
    }
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_framework7_UseJsonConverterDelegateFactory]
=== Use the `JsonConverterDelegate` factory method
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.framework7.UseJsonConverterDelegateFactory`

Replace the `HttpMessageContentConverter.of(..)` factory methods, removed in Spring Framework 7.1, with `JsonConverterDelegate.of(Iterable)`, collecting converters passed individually with `List.of(..)`.

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_framework7_UseSpelParserConfigurationBuilder]
=== Use the `SpelParserConfiguration` builder
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.framework7.UseSpelParserConfigurationBuilder`

Replace the `SpelParserConfiguration` constructors, deprecated in Spring Framework 7.1, with `SpelParserConfiguration.withDefaults()` or the builder API, setting each constructor argument through its named builder method. Constructor calls whose auto-grow flags are not literals are left unchanged.

[#family-spring-modulith2]
== spring › modulith2

*Composite recipes*

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_modulith2_MigrateSpringModulithIncompleteEventPublications_2_2]
=== Migrate Spring Modulith `IncompleteEventPublications` to `FailedEventPublications`
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.modulith2.MigrateSpringModulithIncompleteEventPublications_2_2`

Migrate usages of `IncompleteEventPublications`, deprecated in Spring Modulith 2.2, to `FailedEventPublications`, replacing `resubmitIncompletePublications(ResubmissionOptions)` with `resubmit(ResubmissionOptions)`. It applies to the whole project or not at all, so a project that calls the overloads taking a `Predicate` or a `Duration`, which resubmit every incomplete publication rather than only the failed ones, or that implements `IncompleteEventPublications`, is left unchanged.

_Tags: spring, modulith_

.Recipes applied
[%collapsible]
====
* Change method name (`org.openrewrite.java.ChangeMethodName`)
* Change type (`org.openrewrite.java.ChangeType`)
====

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.modulith.events.IncompleteEventPublications;
import org.springframework.modulith.events.ResubmissionOptions;

class Resubmitter {
    private final IncompleteEventPublications publications;

    Resubmitter(IncompleteEventPublications publications) {
        this.publications = publications;
    }

    void resubmit() {
        publications.resubmitIncompletePublications(ResubmissionOptions.defaults());
    }
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.modulith.events.FailedEventPublications;
import org.springframework.modulith.events.ResubmissionOptions;

class Resubmitter {
    private final FailedEventPublications publications;

    Resubmitter(FailedEventPublications publications) {
        this.publications = publications;
    }

    void resubmit() {
        publications.resubmit(ResubmissionOptions.defaults());
    }
}
----

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_modulith2_FindMigratableIncompleteEventPublications]
=== Find projects whose Spring Modulith `IncompleteEventPublications` usages can be migrated
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.modulith2.FindMigratableIncompleteEventPublications`

Find the Java source files of a project that uses `IncompleteEventPublications` only through `resubmitIncompletePublications(ResubmissionOptions)`, which maps one to one onto `FailedEventPublications.resubmit(ResubmissionOptions)`. A project that calls the overloads taking a `Predicate` or a `Duration`, or implements `IncompleteEventPublications`, does not qualify.

[#io_arconia_rewrite_spring_modulith2_UsePublishedEventAssertMatchingValue]
=== Use `matchingValue` to match a Spring Modulith published event against a value
`io.arconia.rewrite.spring.modulith2.UsePublishedEventAssertMatchingValue`

Replace `PublishedEventAssert.matching(Function, Object)`, deprecated in Spring Modulith 2.1 and removed in 2.2, with `matchingValue(Function, Object)`. Calls passing a `Predicate` keep using `matching`.

*Example*

.Before
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.modulith.test.PublishedEventsAssert.PublishedEventAssert;

class Demo {
    void verify(PublishedEventAssert<OrderCompleted> event) {
        event.matching(OrderCompleted::orderId, "42");
    }

    record OrderCompleted(String orderId) {
    }
}
----

.After
[source,java]
----
import org.springframework.modulith.test.PublishedEventsAssert.PublishedEventAssert;

class Demo {
    void verify(PublishedEventAssert<OrderCompleted> event) {
        event.matchingValue(OrderCompleted::orderId, "42");
    }

    record OrderCompleted(String orderId) {
    }
}
----

import java.util.function.Supplier;

import org.springframework.security.authorization.AuthorizationDecision;
import org.springframework.security.authorization.AuthorizationManager;
import org.springframework.security.core.Authentication;

class AlwaysGranted implements AuthorizationManager<Object> {

    public AuthorizationDecision check(Supplier<Authentication> authentication, Object object) {
        return new AuthorizationDecision(true);

    }
}

[source,java]
----
import java.util.function.Supplier;

import org.springframework.security.authorization.AuthorizationDecision;
import org.springframework.security.authorization.AuthorizationManager;
import org.springframework.security.core.Authentication;

class AlwaysGranted implements AuthorizationManager<Object> {

    @Override
    public AuthorizationDecision authorize(Supplier<Authentication> authentication, Object object) {
        return new AuthorizationDecision(true);
    }

    AuthorizationDecision delegate(AuthorizationManager<Object> manager, Supplier<Authentication> authentication) {
        return manager.authorize(authentication, new Object());
    }
}
----
